描述_ZN: The Tablet of Divine Prophecy of Heaven, erected in 276, the first year of the reign of Wu Tianxi. In 264 A.D., Sun Hao succeeded to the throne of the Three Kingdoms of Wu, and the political situation became more and more dangerous due to his faintness and brutality. 276 A.D., the first year of the reign was changed to Tianxi, and this stone was carved in order to stabilize the people and create the public opinion that the prophecy of God was sent down from the sky, thinking that it was auspicious for Wu. It is said to be the book of the Emperor's elephant, but there is no solid evidence.　　The upper section of the stele is 21 lines long, with 5 characters, 1 line of 6 characters for "imperial decree" and 1 line of 7 characters for "Great Wu"; the middle section is 17 lines long, with 7 characters; the lower section is 10 lines long, with 3, 2 or 1 characters. The original stele was carved at Tianxi Temple in Jiangning (present-day Nanjing). In the sixth year of the Song Dynasty (1091), Hu Zong Shi moved the stele to the rear garden of the transfer department and then to the Jiangning Academy of Scripture, and in the tenth year of the Jiaqing Dynasty (1805), the school official Mao Zao printed the "Jade Sea" in March and the stone was destroyed by fire. The upper part of the original stone has the trek of Hu Zong Shi in the sixth year of Yuan You, the trek engraved by Shi Yu in the first year of Chongning (1102), the trek engraved by Geng Ding in the forty-third year of Jia Jing (1564), and the trek engraved by Weng Fang Gang in the lower part of the stone in the Qing Dynasty, "Beiping Weng Fang Gang Lai Guan".　　The calligraphy of the "Divine Prophecy Tablet of Heaven" was described by Kang Youwei as "amazing and magnificent". The calligrapher wrote the seal script with a clerical style, which is extremely square and heavy at the beginning, square at the turn and round at the inside, and pendulous at the bottom. Huang Boshi of the Song Dynasty said, "In Wu Dynasty, there was the Tian Fa Shen Prophecy Tablet, which was majestic in character if it was in seal script."　　This is the oldest known copy in the collection of the National Palace Museum of the Northern Song Dynasty. The character "Wu" of "Wu County" is slightly damaged at the mouth, while the character "County" is intact, but there are many other slightly damaged strokes. There are more than 200 seals of the Song Dynasty such as "Beihai Kaiguo Lu Xuan's seal" and "Yongbao Wannian".　　The Qing Wang Chang "Jin Shi Zui Jian", Wang Zhuang Hong "additions to the school of monuments," Zhang Yansheng "good book of monuments and posters" and other books recorded.
